predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: San Ignacio Guazú, where three Jesuits began the first reduction in 1609 after the governor of Asunción 'made a deal with the Jesuit Provincial of Paraguay'; Guayrá followed within 22 years

successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: the mission towns left after the expulsion: '89,000 Guaraní in 30 missions' passed to Spanish administration

ledger.x: 1609: three Jesuits begin the first reduction at San Ignacio Guazú.
1632: the Guayrá contest ends with the region deserted; the raiders turned to the Uruguay missions in 1636.
1638: the Tapé missions are gone from the map.
11 March 1641: the Guaraní win at Mbororé.
July 1754: Portuguese and Spanish troops march on the missions.
July 1754: the Spanish side of the joint force (José de Andonaegui) acts against the Guaraní of its own missions to carry out the treaty.
10 February 1756: Caiboaté, the last battle; 'a larger combined force of 3,000 Spanish and Portuguese troops crushed the revolt in 1756'.
1756: the joint campaign ends in the defeat of the Guaraní revolt.

wars.name: Bandeirante raids on the Guaraní missions (to the Battle of Mbororé)
wars.outcome: The bandeirantes emptied Guayrá (12,000 Guaraní moved south by 1632) and invaded the Tapé; the Guaraní militia 'defeated an army of 1,500 or more' at Mbororé on 11 March 1641 and the Uruguay and Paraná missions held.

wars.name: Guaraní War
wars.outcome: Defeat of the Guaraní: Caiboaté on 10 February 1756, the Guaraní driven from the seven missions ceded to Portugal; the Treaty of Madrid was ended by Spain in 1759 and annulled by the Treaty of El Pardo in 1761.

certainty.note: Mission districts in forest and river country with no surveyed frontier; the Guayrá and Tapé extents are the page's descriptions.

The Treaty of Madrid (1750) made the Uruguay River the boundary of the Misiones Orientales ('the land east of it ... went to Portugal'), but it was never fixed on the ground (annulled 1761); everything else stays soft.
